brief.ask: Set the art direction for 6 patriotic evites (Independence Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, Flag Day, stars-and-stripes block party, fireworks) that hosts in other countries can recolor for their own national day.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
Memorial Day is remembrance, not a party: design it with dignity.

proposals.title: The Measure Holds
proposals.idea: Each evite is a scored monument: a single governing light vector at 35° upper-left propagates without re-decision across a classically proportioned plate, foil shimmer, parallax depth, and particle physics, so the invitation reads as one unified architectural event rather than decorated surface.
proposals.geometry: Each plate is divided by a strict golden-section column: the left 38.2% is a deep field (sky, stone, dusk water) carrying structural weight; the right 61.8% is the gathering zone where type, date, and foreground elements resolve. A centered horizontal datum line at the golden mean from the top governs where the primary motif crowns — flag apex, flame tip, star cluster center — so every variant shares one invisible armature. For the phone at 390px, the column snaps to a 4-column grid (1-col gutter, 1-col left field, 2-col right); the datum survives the reflow. The QR link-preview crop is pre-composed as a 1:1 square that contains only the datum line intersection and the event title — never an accidental slice.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — SC caps for event name, tracked +120, set at a size that fills exactly the 61.8% column width so no letter is stranded. Secondary: EB Garamond for venue and time, 13px / 20px leading, flush-left against the column rule. A single weight of IBM Plex Mono (OFL) at 9px is used for the recolor token label ('NATIONAL COLOR A / B / C') so it reads as a production annotation, not decorative type. No decorative script. Case is controlled: event name in full small caps, date in oldstyle figures. Nothing shouts.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plate prompt (one draft grid, 12 variants): 'Cinematic dusk aerial, single motivated key light at 35° upper left, physically accurate volumetric atmosphere, six distinct subjects: (1) field of flags at a military cemetery at golden hour, long raked shadows, (2) monumental stone plaza with crowd silhouettes, (3) harbor with tall ships and fireworks reflection in still water, (4) neighborhood block party table from above, (5) close abstraction of a waving fabric catching single-source side light, (6) night sky with slow long-exposure star trails over an open field — each with identical light direction, muted chroma base suitable for national-color overlay, no faces, no logos, no text.' All plates are treated in post via shader: a luminance mask isolates the key-light highlight zone and locks it to the WebGL foil vector. The image never bleeds to edge; it sits within the
proposals.texture: Simulated cold-press watercolor paper tooth on the plate field — generated via Perlin-noise displacement at 0.4px amplitude over the image, giving the sense that the plate was printed on stock with grain. The right column carries a linen-white ground with a barely perceptible 1pt baseline grid embossed in the paper (visible at 200% zoom, subliminal at 100%). The foil WebGL layer is restricted to the datum line itself and the event-name cap letters: a narrow band of interference-color shimmer that moves with tilt at ±4° max, never spilling into the text column. This is foil as architectural molding, not decoration.
proposals.motion: Sequence is scored like a slow first movement: (1) Plate fades in over 600ms with a gentle luminance bloom originating at the 35°-vector highlight zone — not a flash, an awakening. (2) Foreground cut-out elements (flag, single candle flame, star cluster, depending on occasion) drift into parallax position over 900ms on phone tilt, governed by a spring constant k=0.08 so motion is weighted and deliberate, never bouncy. (3) Foil shimmer activates on first tilt event only, then sustains at 20% opacity resting state. (4) Type resolves last: event name tracks in from 0 letter-spacing to +120 over 400ms — like a cornice sliding into place. Reduced-motion: plate appears at full opacity, no parallax, foil at static 15% opacity, type static. Total perceived load sequence under 1.8 seconds on 4G.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid (12 plates, flat cost) produces the six occasion bases plus alternates. Each plate is imported into Tela as the bottom art layer. A GLSL shader (Plajah-owned, adapted from the WebGL foil system) reads the plate's luminance map and generates: (a) foil shimmer mask locked to the 35° highlight vector, (b) a depth map for parallax ordering of three foreground cut-out layers (near / mid / far). Foreground cut-outs — flag fabric, flame, star burst, paper lantern, sparkler streak — are generated separately via Magnific with a pure white background for clean extraction, then composited in Tela as transparent PNG layers with tilt-reactive spring physics. Live text sits above all layers in Tela's native text engine. Recolor system: three HSL-shift variables (NATIONAL_HUE_A, NATIONAL_HUE_B, ACCENT) exposed as Tela theme tokens; swapping them recolors the plate's luminance o
proposals.humanTrace: The 35° key-light vector is set by editorial decision before any generation begins and held without exception across all twelve plates and all WebGL parameters — it is a human compositional act, not an algorithmic default. The paper-tooth displacement amplitude (0.4px) and the spring constant (k=0.08) are manually tuned against felt experience of weight and pace, the same way a typesetter hand-spaces a titling line. The editorial selection of which six plates advance from the twelve-variant grid is a curatorial judgment about which images carry structural weight at the datum line.
proposals.risk: Cormorant Garamond and a golden-section armature risk reading as 'elegant but cold' to families expecting warmth and festivity. The counter-argument: the foil datum line and the paper-tooth texture provide tactile warmth; the architecture is the gift-wrapping, not the barrier. The deeper risk is that the recolor system, while structurally elegant, requires hosts to trust that swapping three HSL tokens will feel native to their flag's palette — and some national palettes (e.g. high-chroma green and yellow) will stress-test the linen-white ground. This is worth the risk because the alternative — pre-baking national variants — destroys the universality the brief demands.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to announce itself — a dramatic entrance animation, a full-bleed hero moment, a swell before the title appears. I will hold that the reveal must be earned by structure, not announced by gesture: if the datum line and the light vector are set correctly, the eye finds the crown of the motif without being conducted there by a flourish, and that quiet arrival

proposals.title: Ink Pressure, Open Sky
proposals.idea: Each evite is a hand-pressured monoprint — generatively simulated lino or woodblock pull, ink drag, registration slip and all — so the celebration looks like someone stayed up late making it, not a corporation approving it.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone crop. A single dominant plate zone occupies the top 62% — raw block-print territory, bleed to edges, no margin apology. The lower 38% is a torn-paper horizon line (procedurally generated, ragged, not die-cut smooth) that separates the art plate from the live-text zone. No centred grids. No card-inside-a-card framing. The composition leans 4° off vertical, a deliberate press-registration drift that recolour operators keep or correct — their choice, that's the tension.
proposals.typography: Headline: Playfair Display Black, all-caps, letterspacing -0.02em, set at 11vw so it bleeds into the print zone and picks up simulated ink crush on the stems. Subhead / details: Space Grotesk Regular, tracked wide at 0.18em, 13px floor for legibility at 390px. Both OFL. The type sits in the live-text layer, never baked, but its colour is pulled from the dominant ink tone of that card's plate so it reads as part of the same print run. No thin weights — thin weights die in photocopy tests and on cheap OLED.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. The art plate is a Magnific-generated monoprint simulation: one prompt batch returning 8–16 distinct plate variants per holiday theme. Prompt language specifies: single-ink relief print, visible wood grain direction, ink starvation at top-left, over-inking bloom at bottom-right, registration ghost of a second colour shifted 3px southeast. For fireworks and flag themes, the 'second colour' ghost is the shimmer layer that WebGL foil will later inhabit — the ghost is designed in, not added after. Memorial Day plate: charcoal rubbing texture, not ink bloom — slower, quieter, no bloom at all.
proposals.texture: Primary: simulated lino-cut or woodblock pull — Magnific prompt directs paper tooth (140gsm cold-press equivalent), ink drag striations, and a faint emboss shadow at the block edge proving the wood had thickness. Secondary: the torn horizon is a procedural shader tear — not a Photoshop brush, a signed-distance-field edge with fibre fraying, so it responds to zoom without pixelating. WebGL foil layer clings only to the ink-heaviest zones, exactly where a physical foil stamp would bite. It does not smooth; it follows the ridge. Reduced-motion fallback: foil is a static specular highlight baked at 35° key light angle — the decision about where the light is has already been made and cannot be undone without rebuilding the plate.
proposals.motion: Sequence: (1) plate fades in at 0.4s as if a print is being pulled — ink travels top to bottom, opacity builds unevenly. (2) torn horizon tears open left-to-right at 0.6s, revealing live text beneath. (3) foreground cut-outs — a cluster of thematic silhouettes (stars, wheat stalks, a raised fist for Labor Day, poppies for Memorial Day) — drift on gyroscope tilt, parallax depth 3 layers, slowest layer moves 6px per 30° tilt. (4) WebGL foil shimmers on a 2.2s sine loop, amplitude low — a glint, not a disco ball. Memorial Day: no foil loop, no drift speed above 2px, the poppy silhouettes barely move. Everything honours prefers-reduced-motion: cut-outs freeze, foil becomes static specular, tear is instant.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt batch per holiday: 8–16 plate variants, landscape and portrait crops, single-ink and two-ink-ghost versions. Prompt specifies exact print artifact language so the model is directed, not fishing. Best 2–3 plates per holiday selected editorially. Plates import into Tela as the art layer. Torn horizon and foreground silhouettes are SVG paths generated via a SDF shader baked to transparent PNG at 2x — no scan, no photo. WebGL foil and bokeh particles are Plajah's existing shader library, masked to the ink-heavy zones identified in the plate. Live text layer sits above all. Recolour: operators swap the dominant ink tone via a single hue-rotate CSS variable — the foil, the type colour, and the torn-paper edge tint all inherit from it. The 4° registration drift is a CSS transform baked into the plate layer; operators can zero it out or keep it.
proposals.humanTrace: The simulated print artifacts — ink starvation, bloom, registration slip, paper tooth, block-edge emboss shadow — are the human trace. They are not decoration applied after the fact; they are specified in the generative prompt as the primary image logic, which means the Magnific model is being directed to produce evidence of a process, not a result. The 35° key light angle that locks the foil highlight is a committed decision with downstream consequences: change it and the foil, shadow, and parallax order all break. That propagation of consequence is the mark.
proposals.risk: Families opening a party invite might read 'rough print' as cheap or unfinished — the consumer expectation for 'high-end' is gloss, not grain. The risk is worth it because the grain is the argument: it says a person made this for you, not a brand system for a demographic. If the Magnific plate reads as authentic relief print, the roughness becomes warmth. If it reads as failed polish, we lose the room. The direction bets on the prompt craft being precise enough that the artifacts look chosen, not accidental. That bet is the work.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip the registration ghost, the bloom, the torn horizon, and call what remains 'honest.' But removing the evidence of process is not honesty — it is the erasure of the argument. I leave the ink starvation in because the starvation tells you where the press was heavy and where it ran dry, and that specificity is what separates a document from a decoration. proposals.title: Civic Light as a System
proposals.idea: Each evite is a physically-simulated light instrument: one motivated source position per event encodes the emotional register — raking memorial dawn, overhead summer noon, warm block-party dusk — and that single root node propagates without exception into every downstream parameter: foil highlight direction, parallax depth order, particle shadow vector, bokeh scatter axis, and the recolor formula hosts use for their own national day.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 viewport anchored at 390px wide. A strict three-layer spatial stack: background plate at z=0 (sky or field), midground cutout elements at z=1 (flags, silhouettes, flora), foreground particle/bokeh plane at z=2. No decorative borders. The structural grid is a single golden-ratio vertical: 61.8% of the viewport height is the image field; 38.2% is the live-text zone below, separated by a 1px luminous rule whose color is derived from the light-source hue. On tilt, each z-plane parallaxes at a fixed ratio — z0 moves 0px, z1 moves 6px, z2 moves 14px — so the spatial stack is always legible and never collapses into flatness. The Magnific prompt grid targets 2×4 plates (8 variants per event) exploring light-source elevation from 12° to 72° in equal steps, so the art director can select the elevation that best encodes the event's emotional temperature.
proposals.typography: Primary: Space Grotesk (OFL, Google Fonts) — grotesque with just enough geometric tension to read as civic without reading as governmental. Event name set at 32px/1.1 leading, tracked +20, all-caps. Host details (name, date, venue — always live Tela text, never baked) set in Space Grotesk Regular 16px/1.5 leading, sentence case, tracked +5. A secondary accent line uses Playfair Display SC (OFL, Google Fonts) small-caps at 11px for category label (INDEPENDENCE DAY / MEMORIAL DAY etc.) — the one place a serif enters, functioning as a category signal not a decorative gesture. No script. No star-shaped display lettering. Type color is computed from the light-source hue at 95% luminance so it always contrasts the plate without a manual override.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Every plate is a Magnific-generated scene built from a physically-plausible light description: the prompt encodes light-source azimuth, elevation, color temperature, and atmospheric density. Memorial Day prompt forces a single low-raking source at 12° elevation, 5500K, long cast shadows across a field of grass — no crowd, no fireworks, no confetti; the only foreground element is a generative drift of white clover petals at z=2. Flag Day prompt: a cloth-simulation render of a single large flag filling 70% of the plate, light at 45° elevation, fabric fold shadows physically consistent with the source. Fireworks: the plate is dark sky with a single composite burst generated as a particle system render, not a photograph — so the burst direction, shadow, and reflected light on implied crowd silhouettes at z=1 all obey the same source vector. The Magnific grid prompt for the fu
proposals.texture: The plate has zero added texture — the atmosphere is the texture. The WebGL layer adds: (1) a foil shimmer mask applied only to the luminous rule and the event-name type, highlight direction locked to the plate's light-source azimuth; (2) a lens-bokeh scatter of 40–120 particles at z=2, particle size and opacity modulated by tilt input, shadow vector fixed to light source; (3) for Memorial Day only, a candle-flicker shader on a single foreground flame element — flicker frequency 8–12Hz with 15% randomized amplitude, no color shift, only luminance pulse. No noise overlays, no grain filters, no linen textures. The surface is light itself.
proposals.motion: Sequence of states, each triggered by a system input, not an animation timeline. State 0 (load): plate fades in at 400ms ease-out; text slides up 8px over 300ms — nothing else. State 1 (idle): z2 particles drift on a Perlin-noise field, max velocity 0.4px/frame, no looping sparkle. State 2 (tilt): gyroscope input maps to parallax at 60fps; reduced-motion flag disables tilt entirely and substitutes a single 3s breathing ease on z2 opacity (0.7 to 1.0 and back). State 3 (tap): foil shimmer on the luminous rule pulses once — 200ms ease-in, 400ms ease-out — acknowledging the gesture without performing a reveal. Memorial Day: no fireworks, no confetti particles. The candle flicker runs in State 1 at reduced luminance. No autoplay audio, no looping video, no perpetual animation that cannot be paused.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid per event (8 plates, flat cost) directed with precise light descriptions as above. Foreground cutout elements — flag silhouettes, floral sprigs, crowd silhouettes — are generated separately with a transparent-background prompt and composited in Tela as the z=1 layer; they are insignia-free so palette recolor requires only a CSS hue-rotate filter on a hue-isolated layer, no redraw. The WebGL effects layer is a single shared shader file parameterized by four variables exported from each plate's light study: azimuth, elevation, color-temperature, and intensity. The recolor system for international hosts is a Tela palette panel exposing three swatches — primary, secondary, accent — which pipe into the CSS hue-rotate, the shader color-temperature offset, and the foil shimmer tint simultaneously. One panel change recolors the entire evite coherently because every color
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial decisions made by the art director inside the Magnific prompt — the exact elevation angle chosen for each event, the decision to exclude crowd faces, the selection of which of the 8 plates carries the right emotional temperature — are the human trace. The light description in the prompt is a physical argument about feeling: choosing 12° elevation for Memorial Day is a claim about what dignity looks like in light. That claim is visible in the final plate and could not have been arrived at by a model without a human making it.
proposals.risk: The system refuses nostalgia entirely — no bunting, no hand-lettered chalk, no vintage poster grain — and some hosts will read that refusal as coldness. The risk is worth it because the alternative is a glow applied to an old surface, which this team should not ship. If a host finds it cold, the recolor panel and the light-source elevation are the levers they have: a warmer color temperature and a lower elevation produce warmth without importing a historical costume.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a reveal moment — a dramatic entrance animation, a starburst transition, a spectacle that performs the event's emotion. I will argue that a reveal is a one-time event with no rule behind it: after the reveal, the system is inert. proposals.title: Where the Map Was Made
proposals.idea: Each evite is structured as a field-surveyor's document — a generative cartographic plate specific to the host's locality, with coordinate grids, hand-lettered-style notation, and a single dominant landmark silhouette, so that recoloring for another nation's day means substituting a new coordinate origin and a new silhouette, not painting over someone else's iconography.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 (390×844px safe). Primary plate divided by a surveyor's graticule: thin hairline longitude and latitude arcs, not a square grid, so the curvature reads as Earth-specific rather than wallpaper. A centered oval cartouche — the traditional map inset — holds the event title zone. Silhouette of a local landmark bleeds full-width across the lower 38% of the plate, grounding the floating cartographic field above. For Memorial Day the oval becomes a vertical rectangle — a headstone proportion — and the silhouette is a single tree at a distance, not a skyline.
proposals.typography: Headings: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) in italic small-caps — echoes engraved cartographic lettering without costuming as a historical replica. Coordinate annotations and legend text: Source Code Pro (OFL, Google Fonts), 9–11px, tracked wide, uppercase — reads as instrument readout, never decorative. Event details (name, date, venue) live in Tela as Cormorant Garamond Regular, fluid-sized 22–28px. NO ALL-CAPS on event body; sentence case only. Memorial Day: Cormorant Garamond Light, tracked +80, no bold anywhere in that card.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs of people, flags, or trademarked landmarks. The art plate is a generative cartographic illustration: Magnific prompt directed at producing 8–16 plate variants across the six themes — the prompt specifies parchment-ground survey maps with engraved topographic hachures, each variant anchoring a different landmark silhouette type (coastal bluff, inland plain, forested ridge, harbor mouth, urban roofline, open field). Silhouettes are generated as separate transparent-background foreground cut-outs in the Tela foreground layer. The WebGL foil layer is masked to the hairline graticule arcs only — foil lives in the map's coordinate system, not as a decorative wash. Stars (for the block party and fireworks cards) are generative bokeh particles constrained to the sky-zone above the silhouette, not scattered everywhere.
proposals.texture: Simulated cartographic parchment: procedural paper tooth with deliberate foxing spots and ink-bleed at the graticule intersections — these are baked into the generated plate, not a CSS filter. The engraved hachure lines on the silhouette slopes are rendered with slight pressure variation (heavier at the ridge, fading toward the valley floor) to read as a physical burin mark. Foil shimmer on the graticule arcs uses the same 35° upper-left motivated light source direction established by Aria's system — the foil highlight answers to that single origin so it does not contradict the parchment's directional aging.
proposals.motion: Tilt parallax (reduced-motion off): foreground silhouette cut-out drifts 6–9px against the cartographic plate at a 0.4 dampening ratio — the map appears to be a surface you are looking down at from a slight angle. Graticule arcs carry a slow WebGL foil shimmer, 3–5 second cycle, eased sine, never strobing. Fireworks card only: generative particle system above the silhouette, 12–18 simultaneous arcs, each following a ballistic Bézier with a 0.9s hang at apex before dissolving — no looping sparkle rain, each arc fires once per 4s interval. Memorial Day: NO particle motion, NO foil shimmer, NO tilt drift — the card is still. A single candle-flicker WebGL light bleeds from the lower center of the headstone-proportion cartouche, 0.08Hz flicker, barely perceptible. Reduced-motion mode: all motion stops; foil shimmer is replaced by a static specular highlight baked at 35° upper-left.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific batch prompt returns 16 cartographic plate variants (6 themes × 2–3 color-ground options per theme, plus alternates): prompt directed to produce engraved survey-style maps with parchment grounds, topographic hachures, landmark silhouettes as described, at 1200×2600px for downsampling. Silhouettes extracted as separate passes in the same batch using a white-ground variant of the prompt, then composited in Tela as transparent foreground objects. WebGL shader: foil mask drawn from the graticule arc paths exported as SVG from the generative plate, converted to a luminance mask; the 35° highlight vector is a single uniform passed to the shader, not per-element. Particle system for fireworks: procedural GLSL, no pre-rendered sprites. Coordinate text and legend annotations generated procedurally in Tela from the host's actual location data so they are always locally true.
proposals.humanTrace: The hachure lines on the silhouette slopes carry procedurally simulated pressure variation — heavier strokes at the ridge crest, fading toward the base — mimicking the physical behavior of a burin on copperplate. The foxing spots on the parchment ground are placed by a Poisson-disk distribution seeded from a noise field, not uniformly scattered, so they cluster as they do on aged paper. The cartouche oval is slightly imperfect — generated with a 1.5–2.5px radial wobble — so it reads as drawn with a beam compass, not rendered with a CSS border-radius.
proposals.risk: The cartographic frame reads as European colonial survey tradition to many communities for whom maps have been instruments of dispossession. The recolor-for-your-nation mechanic could inadvertently ask a host in a formerly colonized country to celebrate inside a form that historically erased their geography. This risk is worth naming explicitly in the Tela template documentation — the landmark silhouette and coordinate origin must be locally sourced from the host, not pre-filled with a default. The form is worth keeping because the surveyor's document is also the form in which many nations recorded their own geography before and after colonial contact; transformed into a celebration document with the host's own coordinates, it reclaims rather than borrows. But this requires a short onboarding note in the template UI, which I am flagging now.

A cartouche is not a crown; a graticule is not a coat of arms. The Dramatist's instinct to overwhelm with scale and gilding flattens the local into the imperial, which is precisely what a recolo

proposals.title: Light Before the Crowd Arrives
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single theatrical lighting moment — one raking source at a specific angle — that sculpts foreground silhouettes, drives shadow geometry, ignites the foil layer, and resolves into the gathering just as the guest reads their name.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×693px stage. A single vanishing point sits at 58% from top, slightly left of center — never centered, always weighted toward arrival. The composition divides into three acts: sky field (top 38%), event horizon line (a single ruled stroke, 2px, full bleed), and ground plane (bottom 62%). Foreground cut-outs float in forced perspective — closest objects largest and lowest, retreating objects smaller and higher — creating measurable parallax depth on tilt. No card corners, no rounded rect frames: the edge of the phone IS the proscenium.
proposals.typography: Headlines: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — italic for Independence Day, Flag Day, Block Party, Fireworks; small-caps roman for Memorial Day and Labor Day. Size: 44px display, 18px body, 13px metadata. All-caps restricted to the single event-type label only (8px, tracked 0.25em). Body and venue lines: DM Sans (OFL, Google Fonts), regular weight. No centred body text — all lines left-aligned from the vanishing-point vertical. Kerning optically corrected at generation time via Tela's live text engine. Memorial Day headline drops to 36px and loses italic — quieter scale, heavier weight, wider tracking.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Every art plate is a Magnific generative render directed as a lit stage set: physical-simulation sky (volumetric clouds, Rayleigh scattering), procedural crowd silhouettes built from Plajah-owned 3D base meshes, and one dominant practical-light source per card whose angle is declared in the prompt (e.g., 'low southwest sun at 18° elevation, golden hour, hard shadow falling northeast'). The light source angle is the single editorial decision that propagates into every layer: foil UV offset, parallax depth order, shadow direction, bokeh scatter axis. Prompt grid strategy: one Magnific 4×4 prompt per holiday returns 16 sky-and-ground plates at varied times-of-day and crowd densities; editorial selects one hero plate per evite. A second 4×4 prompt generates foreground cut-out elements (flags, lanterns, bunting, tools, flowers, candles) on pure black for easy mask extraction.
proposals.texture: Simulated photochemical grain (8mm film stock emulation, luminance-channel only, 18% opacity) baked into the art plate at generation to prevent sterile CGI read. Foil shimmer on the event-horizon line and any metallic object (buttons, flag grommets, lantern frames) is a WebGL fragment shader: environment-map reflection driven by device gyroscope, gold for warm holidays, silver for Memorial Day. Paper tooth on the type zone: a procedural micro-bump normal map applied to the lower 62% gives the ground plane the feel of heavy cotton stock — visible at 2× retina but not at 1×. Candle flicker shader (Labor Day, Block Party) uses a low-frequency Perlin noise field driving point-light intensity ±15% at 24fps, respecting reduced-motion by collapsing to a static warm glow.
proposals.motion: Sequence is theatrical: curtain up, not carousel. 1) Art plate fades from black in 380ms (ease-in-out, opacity only — no translate, honours reduced-motion at this step). 2) Parallax layer begins passive drift on gyroscope or pointer; closest cut-outs travel 18px at full tilt, farthest 4px — the depth reveals itself only when the guest moves. 3) Foil shader activates at 600ms post-load, sweeps once left-to-right across the event-horizon line in 900ms, then idles to gyroscope. 4) Live text resolves last — each line of copy fades in sequentially, 120ms stagger, bottom-up (venue first, then date, then name, then headline last) — the headline is the final curtain, not the first word. 5) Fireworks evite only: a particle system fires a single burst at 1200ms — one rocket, one bloom, 60 particles, 1.4s decay — then stops. Spectacle is one moment, not a loop. Memorial Day: no particles, no foil s
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids (4×4 each) per holiday = 32 plates per evite for editorial selection. Prompts specify: lighting angle, elevation, season, crowd density, colour temperature, and the instruction 'no flags of specific nations, use abstract bunting geometry only' — enabling recolor by host country without cultural collision. Foreground cut-out elements generated separately on pure black; Plajah pipeline auto-masks via luminance key. WebGL effects layer (foil, grain, bokeh, particles, candle) built as a single reusable GLSL shader stack, parameterized by: primary hue (host recolors this one value), light-source angle (inherited from art plate), and event-type enum. Tela live text handles all name/date/venue fields — never baked. Recolor for another nation's holiday = change primary hue parameter + swap bunting geometry cut-out + re-run one 2×4 Magnific prompt for sky plate at new co
proposals.humanTrace: The light-source angle — declared as a specific degree value (18°, 35°, 67°) for each holiday — is the human editorial act. Every downstream decision (shadow direction, foil offset, parallax depth order, bokeh axis) is computed from that one number. The angle is chosen for emotional reason: Memorial Day gets the narrowest, lowest morning light (12°) because grief is specific and early; Independence Day gets high summer noon (72°) because it is unambiguous and hot; Labor Day gets late-afternoon oblique (35°) because the day is almost over and the work was real. That editorial reasoning — emotional, not algorithmic — is the sign of a human hand in the machine.
proposals.risk: The bottom-up text reveal (venue before headline) will feel wrong to every stakeholder on first review. They will ask to flip it. The risk is worth it because the headline arriving last — after the guest has already read where and when — makes it land as confirmation rather than announcement; the guest already feels invited before they read the word 'celebrate.' Losing that sequence collapses the theatrical timing into a poster. The second risk: directing Magnific to avoid nation-specific flag imagery may produce generic or sterile results in early grids; mitigation is to specify abstract geometric forms (stripes, stars as five-point geometry, chevrons) and over-generate, selecting only plates where the abstraction reads as festive rather than institutional.

That is a decision about how little to feel, not about restraint. A family opening this link on a summer evening deserves a moment that rises to the occasion of their gathering. proposals.title: One Flag. One Field. Six Days.
proposals.idea: A single architectural silence — a vast, generative field of negative space bisected by one load-bearing stripe or symbol — is the identity system; every holiday shifts only the geometry of that one element, so the host's recolor is a single hue swap on a structure that already holds.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, full-bleed vertical. The plate is divided by a single horizon line placed at the golden ratio (≈241px from top on a 390×690 art plate). Above: pure field, color-swappable. Below: a 1px hairline that expands, on tilt, into the event's one symbol — a folded-corner flag for Memorial Day, a radiating star grid for Independence Day, a single torch silhouette for Labor Day, a canton rectangle for Flag Day, a block of rowhouse geometry for the block party, a single chrysanthemum-burst circle for fireworks. The symbol never fills more than 22% of the plate area. Foreground cut-outs (drifting sparks, a single leaf, confetti squares) occupy the upper field only, never crossing the hairline. Live text sits in a locked 48px bottom reserve, set flush-left, never centered.
proposals.typography: Instrument Serif (OFL, Google Fonts) for the event name — tracked to +120, uppercase, 18px, weight Regular — so it reads as inscription, not announcement. The date and venue in Space Grotesk Light 13px, natural case, 1.6 line-height. No display headline. The name of the day is the largest type on the card and it is still quiet. For recolor markets: the type structure does not change; only the field hue above the hairline changes.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. The art plate is a Magnific-generated abstract field: a single Magnific prompt grid (8 plates) produces the six holidays plus two alternates. Prompt direction: 'extreme close-up of woven textile fiber, lit from a single raking light source at 15 degrees, fiber direction horizontal, no pattern, no color, monochrome output — the color is applied in Tela as a multiply layer.' The textile read gives human trace without a photo shoot. The symbol geometry is a Tela vector mask cut into the textile plate, revealing a WebGL foil shimmer layer beneath — so the symbol glows from inside the field rather than sitting on top of it.
proposals.texture: Woven textile fiber, generatively rendered: the fiber tooth is visible at 1x but resolves to a near-flat field at thumbnail scale (link preview, QR context). No grain added on top — the fiber IS the grain. The hairline is rendered at 0.5px (device-pixel-ratio 2) so it reads as a physical incision. Foil shimmer on the symbol is a WebGL shader, physically plausible single-light-source, not rainbow — the foil shifts between the field color and white only.
proposals.motion: Three-phase, gyroscope-driven, reduced-motion-respected. Phase 1 (load, 0–0.4s): the hairline draws from left to right at constant velocity — no easing, architectural. Phase 2 (idle): the symbol behind the hairline breathes via a 0.003-opacity foil pulse, 4s loop, imperceptible unless you look for it. Phase 3 (tilt): foreground cut-outs (sparks / leaf / confetti) drift in parallax on the Z-axis above the hairline; the symbol's foil shimmer intensifies with tilt angle, max 18% brightness increase. Nothing crosses the hairline. Reduced-motion: hairline is pre-drawn, foil is static at 40% opacity, no parallax drift.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid, 8–16 plates, textile-fiber direction: produces the base art for all six holidays plus alternates. Tela layers: (1) generated textile plate as base, hue-rotatable; (2) vector mask for the symbol, cut into the plate, revealing WebGL foil shader; (3) foreground cut-out layer — procedurally generated sparks/confetti via GLSL particle shader seeded differently per holiday; (4) live text layer, locked bottom 48px reserve. The hairline is a Tela vector element, 0.5px, color inherits from field hue at 60% luminance. Recolor export: host changes one HSL hue value on the field layer; hairline, foil, and type shift automatically via Tela's relative color tokens. No re-generation required.
proposals.humanTrace: The woven textile fiber — generatively rendered but physically plausible raking light, visible fiber crimp, directional tooth — is the sign of making. The foil shimmer obeys a single light source position consistent across all six cards, so the collection reads as one object photographed under one lamp, not six separate renders.
proposals.risk: The risk is that families and civic groups read 'quiet' as 'cold' — that the restraint registers as indifference rather than dignity. That risk is worth carrying because the one element that does move (the hairline drawing, the foil breathing) earns its weight precisely because everything else is silent; a card that is 90% empty and 10% alive is more surprising at phone-open than one that fires everything at once. The Memorial Day card in particular cannot afford to be festive — this system gives it dignity without a separate design language.

I disagree specifically: the foil shimmer is the crescendo; it is just deferred until the guest tilts the phone, which means the host earns the drama by the act of looking. disputes.objection: The bottom-up text reveal — venue first, date second, name third, headline last — inverts the hierarchy of reading so completely that the work refuses to be legible until it has performed itself, and a composition that withholds its primary information behind a theatrical sequence is not building tension, it is delaying resolution; the Pantheon does not make you wait for the oculus. The vanishing point at 58% from top, slightly left of center, is declared as a compositional weight but is then immediately contradicted by cut-outs floating in forced perspective that pull the eye in multiple directions simultaneously — there is no single governing measure from which the other decisions hang, on
disputes.concession: The decision to declare the light-source angle as a specific degree value per holiday — 12° for Memorial Day, 72° for Independence Day — and to propagate that single number into foil offset, shadow direction, parallax order, and bokeh axis is exactly the kind of governing constraint I have come to t

disputes.objection: The textile fiber is the grain and the symbol is the foil and the hairline is the incision — I hear all that, but every decision cancels the next one out until there is nothing left to argue with; a civic occasion has pressure and mess and the woven field absorbs all of it into one long exhale of negative space, which is not restraint, it is avoidance dressed as discipline; the symbol never fills more than 22% of the plate and nothing crosses the hairline and the foil only shifts between field color and white — this work has built itself a perfect room where nothing can go wrong, and I distrust a room like that.
disputes.concession: The 0.5px hairline rendered as a physical incision is right — that one decision carries more weight than most of the decoration in the other proposals, and I would steal it.

disputes.objection: The light-source angle is declared as an emotional editorial act — grief gets 12°, jubilation gets 72° — but emotion is not a system rule; it is a caption written after the fact. The angle must propagate correctly into foil UV offset, parallax depth order, and shadow geometry regardless of whether the number was chosen for feeling or physics, which means the emotional framing is decoration on top of the actual constraint, not the constraint itself. Worse, the vanishing point at 58% from top with crowd silhouettes built from 3D base meshes is a screensaver with a theatrical rationale — spectacle dressed as architecture.
disputes.concession: The insistence that one declared light-source angle is the single editorial decision from which every downstream parameter — foil offset, shadow direction, bokeh axis — must be computed without exception is exactly the correct systems logic, and I will take that rule seriously even if the Baroque Dr

disputes.objection: The woven textile fiber prompt is the proposal's most serious problem: 'no pattern, no color, monochrome output — the color is applied in Tela as a multiply layer' describes a generic fiber with no location, no maker tradition, no weave structure that belongs to any specific place or people — and the proposal calls this a human trace. It is not. It is texture-as-mood, which is exactly the flattening I object to: a woven surface pressed into service as atmosphere without anyone asking whose loom, whose fiber count, whose selvage. The universalism the Minimalist mistakes for restraint is just unattributed specificity with the labels removed.
disputes.concession: The hairline that draws at constant velocity — no easing, architectural — is genuinely disciplined pacing: it earns its silence because it refuses to perform arrival, and that refusal is a real editorial position I respect.

disputes.objection: The hairline that expands into a symbol is being called a reveal, but a reveal requires a before and an after that differ in emotional register — here the before is silence and the after is slightly less silence, which is not drama but postponement. The symbol capped at 22% of the plate is a decision dressed as a principle: when the emotion of the occasion is Independence Day or a neighborhood block party, that economy is not restraint, it is refusal — the scale does not match the feeling, and no system rule changes that mismatch. I will grant that the woven textile fiber as the image logic is genuinely interesting — it gives the field a material body without a photograph — but the rest of t
disputes.concession: The woven textile fiber as the sole image logic — monochrome, raking light, color applied as a multiply layer — is the most honest human trace on the table: it gives the field weight and temperature without pretending to be something it is not.

disputes.objection: The cartouche, the graticule arcs, the parchment foxing, the hachure pressure variation, the radial wobble on the oval — each element is individually justified but collectively they form a museum of justifications, and a museum is not a composition; when every texture has a reason the silence has none, and without silence there is no hierarchy, only inventory. The foil confined to the graticule arcs sounds like discipline but is actually the opposite: it decorates the structure rather than revealing it, which means the structure was never load-bearing to begin with. I would ask what single contrast carries the meaning and find that the proposal cannot answer, because it has already spent eve
disputes.concession: The headstone-proportion cartouche for Memorial Day is a genuine structural decision — proportion doing emotional work without a single added element, which is exactly the kind of edit I would protect.

synthesis.direction: Each evite is built on a single declared light-source angle — chosen for emotional reason before generation begins — that propagates without exception into every downstream parameter: foil UV offset, parallax depth order, shadow vector, bokeh scatter axis, and the recolor formula. Portrait 9:16 at 390px, three spatial layers (z=0 plate, z=1 cutout silhouettes, z=2 particles), golden-ratio vertical split between image field and live-text zone, separated by a 1px luminous rule whose color is computed from the light-source hue. Type in Space Grotesk (OFL) with a single Playfair Display SC (OFL) accent line as category signal — no script, no star-shaped display faces. Magnific prompt grids specify light-source azimuth, elevation, color temperature, and atmospheric density; one 8-plate grid per event, flat cost, directed with precise physical-light language so the model is given an argument, not a mood. Memorial Day receives a 12° raking dawn source, no particles, no foil loop, no crowd — only a candle-flicker shader at reduced luminance and white clover petals drifting at z=2. Motion is state-driven, not timeline-driven: load, tilt, tap, reduced-motion — the system is alive for as long
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Rebellious Hand's ink-starvation-and-bloom logic — the idea that the generative prompt should specify evidence of a physical process, not just a result — survives as the guiding language for Magnific prompt craft: each plate prompt must describe the light in terms of what it does to a surface (grazes, blooms, starves, rakes) so the model produces physically-committed images, not atmosphere-as-mood.
synthesis.editorCut: The Radical Minimalist removed the bottom-up text reveal sequence (the Baroque Dramatist's venue-first, headline-last theatrical stagger) and the 4° registration-drift CSS transform from the Rebellious Hand. Both were editorial gestures performing arrival rather than encoding structure. The Minimalist's rule: if removing it does not break the light system, it does not belong in the system. synthesis.openDecision: Memorial Day: the candle-flicker shader requires a single foreground flame element at z=1 — does that element exist in Plajah's owned 3D asset library, or does it need to be generated as a separate Magnific pass on a transparent background? That determines whether Memorial Day ships in the first production run or holds for a second prompt grid.
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team agreed on one thing before anything else: the light-source angle must be declared by a human, for an emotional reason, before a single generation runs — and then held without exception across every layer. Where they split was on what that discipline should look like at the surface. The Futurist wanted the system to be the experience: no nostalgia, no grain, no vintage grammar, just physically-plausible light doing all the feeling. The Rebellious Hand pushed back hard, arguing that a system with no evidence of process reads as corporate even when the physics are correct — that the prompt itself needs to specify what light does to a surface, not just where it comes from. I took that argument seriously and kept it, because it changes how we write the Magnific prompts, which changes what the model returns.

The Baroque Dramatist wanted the reveal — the theatrical sequence, the curtain-up, the headline arriving last. The Radical Minimalist wanted the hairline and the silence. I sided with the Minimalist's cut: the bottom-up text stagger and the registration drift are gestures that perform arrival rather than encode structure, and this system does not need to announce itself. The text resolves in reading order. The structure is the announcement.

The World-Eclectic Traveler raised the most important flag in the room: the cartographic frame carries colonial history that some hosts will not be able to separate from the celebration. That warning lives in the Tela template documentation regardless of which direction ships. It is not a design decision — it is a responsibility the team named and I am passing to you.

The one thing I cannot resolve for you is whether Plajah's 3D asset library already contains a candle flame element suitable for Memorial Day's z=1 layer. That answer determines whether the full collection ships together or whether Memorial Day holds. Everything else is ready to generate.

quotes.line: Choosing 12° elevation for Memorial Day is a claim about what dignity looks like in light. That claim is visible in the final plate and could not have been arrived at by a model without a human making it.
The prompt specifies evidence of a process, not a result — which means the Magnific model is being directed to produce evidence of a process, not a result. That bet is the work.
